text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 26 in history.
1440 - Gilles de Rais, who fought for Joan of Arc and was made Marshal of France, was hanged after being accused of satanism and murder.
1685 - Giuseppe Domenico Scarlatti born. Italian composer and son of Alessandro Scarlatti, his fame is based on his keyboard sonatas of which he wrote over 550.

1759 - Georges Jacques Danton born. French revolutionary leader who played a leading role in the overthrow of the monarchy. However he fell victim to the ensuing Reign of Terror and was guillotined in 1794.
1825 - The Erie Canal was opened to traffic. An historic waterway that extended from Buffalo to Albany, New York and connected Lake Erie with the Hudson River.

1881 - After long-standing bad feelings between the Clanton family and the Earp family, Wyatt Earp and two of his brothers and "Doc" Holliday gunned down two Clantons and two other men at the O.K. Corral in Tombstone, Arizona.
1896 - The Treaty of Addis Ababa signed, establishing peace between Italy and Abyssinia (Ethiopia) and recognising Abyssinian independence.
1905 - Revolutionary Russian workers in St.Petersburg formed the first Soviet (assembly) in brief uprising.
1905 - A Treaty of Separation between Norway and Sweden was signed and King Oscar II of Norway abdicated.
1916 - Francois Mitterrand born. He was elected France's first socialist president in May 1981.
1919 - Mohammed Reza Pahlavi born. Shah of Iran from 1941 until 1979 when he was deposed after exiled Ayatollah Khomeini returned to Iran to lead an Islamic Revolution.
1955 - South Vietnam was proclaimed a republic by Ngo Dinh Diem who declared himself president and executive head of the government.
1967 - The Shah of Iran was officially crowned on his 48th birthday having deferred his coronation for 26 years.
1979 - South Korean President Park Chung-Hee was shot and killed by his intelligence chief Kim Jae-kyu.
1990 - The Soviet republic of Kirghizia decided to change its official name to the Socialist Republic of Kyrgyzstan, a title recalling the ancient Turkic origins of many of its people.
1994 - Israel and Jordan sign a peace treaty in a ceremony at their border attended by U.S. President Bill Clinton.
1995 - Russian President Boris Yeltsin was in hospital after suffering his second mild heart attack in less than four months.
